non_claims: methoxy versus methylenedioxy substitution and the biaryl and ring stereochemistry (schisandrin B versus gomisin N) are not resolved
dibenzocyclooctadienes with a C6, C7 or C9 hydroxyl or ester lose water or the acid first and are not covered by these terms

precursors acquired as [M+NH4]+ (listed with [M+H]+ in Shi 2009 Table 3) are not covered: the losses are computed from the hypothesis precursor, while the products follow NH3 loss, so the rule costs recall there

under the common [M+Na]+ hypothesis each sodiated precursor and its loss targets lie 2.4 mDa from those of the [M+H]+ of a composition with C2 for NaH (deoxyschisandrin vs C26H30O6, such as kurarinone), inside both tolerances, so these protonated compounds are tested against the losses

notes: Schisandra dibenzocyclooctadienes without a ring hydroxyl or ester lose C5H10 (base) and then a methoxyl radical (C6H13O in total) from [M+H]+ (Huang 2007, Shi 2009); the second ion is a radical-loss product of the first, so one ring cleavage is shown and the rule is not measured.

competitors.note: Phyltetralin (aryltetralin with two methoxymethyl groups) is C24H32O6 like deoxyschisandrin; no cited source reports its positive-mode ions, so it is declared for the competitor FPR.
